brief: Dovish NY Fed signals (Williams: at most one more hike this year, no urgency to act) reversed a hawk-driven run-up in October hike odds (to 75%), pulling the dollar higher and giving gold a bid, even as the long end sold off on Treasury supply (Paramount Skydance's $52bn bond deal, with a $32bn tranche currently sold) and seasonal weakness, steepening the curve back to pre-FOMC levels and pushing 30Y yields to 5.61%, the highest since 2002. Oil fell (WTI back below $90, futures down over 3%) on a cluster of de-escalation signals around the Strait of Hormuz: Qatar-mediated talks, Saudi Arabia restoring about half its East-West pipeline capacity, an IEA reserve-release stance plus a US offer of up to 40 million SPR barrels, and a reported (and denied) US plan to ease Russia sanctions, even though Iran had struck a tanker in the Strait and threatened to block regional exports if its security is not ensured. Equities split: Nasdaq alone gained on AI-linked strength (Oracle, Sonnet 5.5) while breadth worsened, NYSE new lows beating new highs for a tenth straight day. Bitcoin's bounce came with falling leverage, per Glassnode.
